name: dsh-orch-lite
description: Agent preset that keeps the main session orchestrating: one continuable agent per feature branch, each owning a git work area (.worktrees/<feature_id>) allocated by the orch_tool work-area tool; explore agents for wide read-only sweeps (the platform decides continuability by provider; no backgroundMode config exists); a lazy git-repository bootstrap when a write task lands in a fresh folder (bootstraps the minimum repo in the session's own working folder — git init -b main plus a baseline commit of all existing files, with a secret safety net written to .gitignore — with the walk-up check as the only nesting defense); the gate denies the main session exactly two things — writes inside a worker lane, and shell commands whose effects leave the repository (push, publish, gh) — and requires every subagent / subagent_fork dispatch to carry a fenced-JSON package (feature_id / objective / acceptance_criteria / worktree + handbook pointer); explore carries no package. The coordinator states a serial/parallel dependency plan right after each task routing line (任务 @feature/<fid> · [A, B] · A → B · [A, B] → C · [A → C, B → D]); parallelism is the default, only a shared file or a true output dependency serializes. orch_tool carries create/merge/remove plus two read-only diagnostics: list (every work area and every feature branch without one) and doctor (dirty areas, stale areas, bypassed commits). The two manuals and the tool are published globally, so every preset can use them; the enforcement (protocol section, worker hint, gate) stays scoped to this preset.
